LD 207 3: An Act to Add Positions to the Maine State Police
Executive Protection Unit
Testimony of Rep. Matt Moonen, Portland V February 9, 2026
Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus, and honorable members of the ]oint Standing Committee on Criminal Iustice and Public Safety, thank you for the opportunity to
present LD 207 3: An Act to Add Positions to the Maine State Police Executive
Protection Unit.
Threats to elected officials are on the rise, both in Maine and across the country. Last year, Pennsylvania Governor ]osh Shapiro was the target of an assassination attempt at his official residence, which was set on fire while the Governor and his family slept inside. Several months later, former Speaker of the Minnesota House of Representatives Melissa Hortman and her husband were murdered in a horrific attack that also left another lawmaker and his wife seriously injured.
There have also been several high-profile attempts on President Trump's life, including the
july 2024 assassination attempt in Butler, Pennsylvania, that left one member of the public
dead and two others injured.
Threats of violence are certainly on our minds here in Maine, and we have taken steps to
keep elected officials and those around them safe -- for example, by taking steps to secure the Cross Office Building, among other measures.
LD 2073 would continue our work to improve security by adding two positions to the
Executive Protection Unit, a dedicated group charged with protecting Maine's Governor. These professionals do an incredible job with the resources they have, but at this time,
there are just six of them working to cover every hour of the day, every day of the year.

meaningful increase in staffing levels to ensure the Executive Protection Unit has the resources they need to keep the next Governor and their family safe and to protect our i

Statement in support of
L.D. 2073, An Act to Add Positions to the Maine State Police Executive Protection Unit
Joint Standing Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety
February 9, 2026
Senator Beebe Center, Representative Hasenfus, and honorable members of the Criminal Justice and Public Safety Committee. My name is Scott Stewart. I am the Chief of the Brunswick Police Department, and the president of the Maine Chiefs of Police Association. I am providing testimony on behalf of the Association in support of LD 2073.
The Maine Chiefs of Police Association's mission is straightforward: to strengthen the working relationships among Maine's police leaders, to promote professionalism and consistent standards across the state, and to support the men and women who serve our communities every day. At the heart of that mission is a shared commitment to protecting life and property and upholding the values of our profession.
This bill proposes adding two State Police Detective positions to the Executive Protection Unit within the Department of Public Safety. While these positions do not directly increase staffing or funding for municipal police departments, the Maine Chiefs of Police view LD 2073 as a meaningful and necessary investment in the overall safety of our state.
The Executive Protection Unit is charged with protecting the Governor, the Governor's family, and any additional individuals designated by the Governor or the Department. Its members receive advanced training in personal protection, physical security, and threat

assessment. The unit also works in close partnership with state, local, and federal agencies to ensure comprehensive security for the Governor and for visiting dignitaries.
The work of the EPU extends far beyond individual protection. It is essential to maintaining continuity of government, sustaining public confidence, and ensuring that state leaders can perform their duties safely and without interruption. In recent years, the demands placed on this unit have increased significantly in both volume and complexity. Threat assessments, public event security, and rapid response capabilities all require specialized expertise and sufficient staffing.
When the Executive Protection Unit is understaffed, the strain is felt across Maine's entire law enforcement community. Municipal departments are frequently asked to fill gaps, assist with protective details, or respond to threats involving state officials. These responsibilities, while important, pull local officers away from community policing and core public safety functions.
By adding these two detective positions, LD 2073 strengthens the State Police's ability to meet its executive protection responsibilities without shifting additional burdens onto municipal agencies. This investment will enhance coordination, improve threat management, and contribute to a safer environment for both the public and the officers who serve them.
For these reasons, the Maine Chiefs of Police Association respectfully urges the Committee to support LD 2073.

the Maine State Police Executive Protection Unit." Our agency position is reflective of the fact these positions are not

Previously in my career, I served as the Commanding Officer of the Maine State Police Executive Protection
Unit (EPU). Currently, I serve as the State Police Major of Support Services and supervise the current Commander of
the EPU. My testimony will be general in nature and not specific, due to the sensitive nature of the EPU's mission.
Maine's Executive Protection Unit was formed on July 9, 1957, after Governor Ed Muskie received a threat to his life. The EPU was tasked then, as it is today, with providing security for the Governor of the State of Maine, the Governor's immediate family and dignitaries visiting Maine.

The threat environment in 2026 is significantly more complex than it was in 1957. At that time, threats to public officials were less frequent, news cycles were slower, technology was limited, and official schedules were less publicly known. Security often relied primarily on a visible physical presence to deter malicious intent. Today, EPU members are tasked with threat mitigation at a level previously never imagined, let alone experienced. Nationally, politically motivated threats and attacks are increasingly common, and Maine is not immune. The EPU operates in a world of constant risk assessment, and those assessments now require a higher level of security than in years past. As a result, members are being tasked to work more, travel more, and assume greater personal risk in order to complete their mission. They are professionals and do so without complaint.
The EPU's primary mission is to protect the Governor and what that office represents to the State of Maine. The unit protects the position, not the individual holding it. Just as with our current Governor, any future Governor will receive the highest level of security the unit can provide, using the resources made available to it.
